mir_eval.style: Brief project introduction and documentation gateway (reStructuredText)
mir_eval.structure: Badges → purpose → external documentation → dependencies → citation.
mir_eval.example: No runnable API example in the root README. Installation and usage are delegated to linked documentation.
mir_eval.data: No concrete sample arrays, shapes, time units or file contract in the root README.
mir_eval.strength: Quick orientation and clear navigation to the maintained reference.
mir_eval.barrier: An agent limited to the root README needs another source for executable usage and input contracts.
mir_eval.check: Compare root-only references with the local docs supplied to A1; inspect input-shape and unit failures at the API level.

Thumbnailator.style: Benefits and a fluent task example, followed by reference links (Markdown)
Thumbnailator.structure: Release information → what/why → thumbnail workflow → features/examples/API links → license.
Thumbnailator.data: Placeholder directory of images; maximum pixel dimensions, aspect-ratio behavior and JPEG output are explained. The example does not supply an actual fixture directory.
Thumbnailator.strength: A compact, recognizable end-to-end task demonstrates fluent call order and intended output.
Thumbnailator.barrier: The root example does not specify every low-level receiver, helper, visibility constraint or exception contract. A1 also receives built Javadocs.
Thumbnailator.check: Use the recorded Pipeline/Rotation constructor contradiction and invented helper/getter failures to separate wrong generated guidance from audience-model mistakes; do not attribute the A1/A2 gap to style alone.

tslearn.style: Data-first onboarding tutorial and feature catalog (Markdown)
tslearn.structure: Installation → getting data into shape → preprocessing → training/prediction → feature table → documentation → contribution/citation.
tslearn.example: Explicit Python time-series lists → to_time_series_dataset → scaling → KNeighborsTimeSeriesClassifier.fit/predict; expected labels are displayed.
tslearn.data: Explains 3D NumPy shape (n_ts, max_sz, d), variable-length series and concrete synthetic lists with labels.
tslearn.strength: Connects input representation, preprocessing and a complete model workflow with a visible expected result.
tslearn.barrier: A tutorial covers selected workflows; it does not establish contracts for all 235 frozen API names or optional estimators.
tslearn.check: Separate tutorial-covered APIs from the wider manifest; inspect failures involving array shape, fitted state and optional dependencies.

MDAnalysis.style: Scientific overview, domain workflow and documentation navigation (reStructuredText)
MDAnalysis.structure: Simulation-analysis overview → community/governance → example analysis → installation/docs → contribution/citation.
MDAnalysis.example: mda.Universe('topol.tpr', 'traj.trr') → select_atoms('name OH') → positions/velocities/forces → trajectory iteration and center_of_mass().
MDAnalysis.data: Names a topology/trajectory pair using TPR/TRR extensions. These are placeholder files, not the study's checked-in fixture paths; the root example does not fully describe shapes, units or available trajectory fields.
MDAnalysis.strength: Shows the central Universe/AtomGroup/trajectory relationship and a meaningful scientific workflow.
MDAnalysis.barrier: An agent still needs valid paired files, selections and available attributes. The A1 bundle additionally includes local Sphinx sources and a hosted-doc snapshot.
MDAnalysis.check: Audit actual fixture formats, topology/trajectory compatibility and field availability separately from README style. Generated/repair documents remain snapshot evidence while the pipeline runs.

RDPro.style: System-component map and navigation (Markdown; pinned Beast source)
RDPro.structure: System overview → spatial data and IO → visualization → raster/vector processing → synthetic-data generator → installation/developer/data links.
RDPro.example: No executable API workflow in the root README. Usage and setup are delegated to beast/doc.
RDPro.data: Lists spatial formats including Shapefile, CSV, JSON/WKT and GeoJSON; detailed loading and environment instructions are in linked local documents.
RDPro.strength: Explains how the system's capabilities fit together and points to task-specific documentation.
RDPro.barrier: A root-only reader lacks executable receiver/data setup. The historical documented-88 cohort refers to the full original bundle, not this README alone.
RDPro.check: Keep historical 171-entry results separate from the new validated 161-API study. The reused generated file has 171 entry headings; its 10 extra entries are outside the new experiment manifest. New v5 has no scheduled A1 rerun; its original documentation is inspected as context.
